reason: The cited evidence shows that annealing can induce chemical ordering (E2) and that HEAs can be BCS superconductors with electron-phonon coupling (E1, E3), but none of the passages provide direct support for the key mechanistic links: that SRO causes lattice softening, that this softening enhances electron-phonon coupling, or that the as-cast state suppresses superconductivity relative to the annealed state.
premises: Annealing at ~0.5 Tm induces short-range chemical ordering (SRO) in the target HEA
SRO formation causes localized lattice softening
Localized lattice softening enhances electron-phonon coupling
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling triggers superconductivity in the annealed state
The as-cast disordered state lacks these features and suppresses superconductivity
